name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island
note: 23 km impact crater in a polar desert; rover and EVA field tests since 1997.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Beacon Valley)
program: NASA and NSF Mars-analog field studies
note: Coldest, driest ice-free desert; ice-cemented permafrost under dry soil.

name: Atacama Desert hyperarid core (Yungay)
note: Driest non-polar desert; salt-rich, nearly sterile soils.

name: Death Valley (Badwater Basin)
program: Mars rover and instrument field tests
note: Salt pans, alluvial fans and volcanic craters within a day's drive.

name: Mauna Kea upper slopes
note: Fine volcanic tephra under dry, high-UV skies.

name: HI-SEAS habitat site, Mauna Loa
note: Barren lava flows with lava tubes at 2,500 m; crew isolation studies.

name: Askja and Holuhraun lava fields
note: Fresh basalt and pumice desert in the rain shadow of Vatnajökull.

name: Craters of the Moon
note: Young basalt flows, cinder cones and lava tubes.

name: Meteor Crater (Barringer)
note: 1.2 km simple impact crater, exceptionally well preserved.

name: Black Point Lava Flow
program: NASA Desert RATS rover and EVA tests
note: Basalt flow and cinder terrain used for pressurized-rover traverses.

name: Sudbury impact structure
note: Giant ancient impact basin; forested today, so a geology-only analog.

name: Nördlinger Ries
note: 24 km impact crater with suevite breccia; farmland today.

name: Río Tinto
note: Acidic, iron- and sulfate-rich river system, like Meridiani's jarosite.

name: Mars Desert Research Station (Hanksville)
note: Jurassic mudstones and sandstones around a simulated-mission habitat.

name: Bockfjorden volcanoes, Svalbard
note: Volcanic vents with carbonate deposits like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001.

name: Axel Heiberg Island cold springs
note: Perennial springs flowing through thick permafrost and gypsum domes.

name: Lanzarote (Timanfaya and La Corona tubes)
note: Recent basalt fields and long lava tubes; ESA's astronaut geology classroom.

name: Lonar Crater
note: Rare impact crater in flood basalt, like many lunar mare craters.

name: Pilbara (Dresser Formation)
note: 3.5-billion-year-old stromatolites; a template for ancient Martian life.

name: El Pinacate volcanic field
note: Maar craters and cinder cones in the Sonoran Desert.

name: Dumont Dunes (Mojave)
note: Steep sand dunes used to test Mars rover wheels.

name: Concordia Station (Dome C)
note: Small crew isolated through months of polar darkness; ESA's 'White Mars'.

name: Lava Beds National Monument
note: Hundreds of lava tubes, some holding year-round ice.

name: Makhtesh Ramon (D-MARS)
note: Erosion cirque in the Negev; site of a month-long simulated Mars mission.

name: Dallol, Danakil Depression
note: Hot, hyper-acid, hypersaline springs: a limit-of-life test bed.

name: Arkaroola
note: Ancient sediments and hydrothermal sites in the arid Flinders Ranges.

name: White Sands gypsum dunes
note: Largest gypsum dunefield, comparable to gypsum dunes near Mars's north pole.

name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
program: Lighting analog for the lunar south pole
note: Around the equinoxes the Sun circles the horizon, as it does at Shackleton's rim.

name: Mistastin Lake impact structure
note: Impact melt in anorthosite, the rock of the lunar highlands.

name: Stillwater Complex (Beartooth Mountains)
note: Anorthosite and norite layers, rocks close to the lunar highland crust.

name: Tibesti Mountains (Trou au Natron)
note: Hyperarid shield volcanoes and calderas, like a small Tharsis.

name: Dasht-e Lut (Gandom Beryan and yardangs)
program: Satellite studies of extreme surface heat
note: Hottest land surface measured from orbit; giant wind-carved yardangs.

name: Waw an Namus volcano
note: Black tephra halo around a caldera in the hyperarid Sahara.

name: Harrat Khaybar lava field
note: Vast young basalt field in the desert, with long lava tubes.

name: Qaidam Basin (Dalangtan playa)
note: High, cold, salty desert with sulfates and yardangs.

name: Salar de Uyuni
note: World's largest salt flat and one of the flattest places on Earth.

name: Ojos del Salado high Puna
note: Highest volcano on Earth: thin air, intense UV and permafrost.

name: Tso Kar basin, Ladakh
note: Cold, high, salty basin at 4,500 m.

name: Tolbachik lava fields, Kamchatka
note: Fresh basalt flows on cold, permafrost ground.

name: Wolfe Creek Crater
note: Fresh 880 m impact crater in the arid outback.

name: Undara lava tubes
note: Some of the longest lava tubes on Earth.

name: Peary Land
note: Northernmost ice-free land: polar desert on continuous permafrost.

name: Lunar Crater Volcanic Field
note: Maar craters and cinder cones in the Great Basin desert.
